description: Survey competition page and existing artifacts to decide what to do next
steps: Step 1: Search for current competition status and rules at https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/kaggle-measuring-agi/overview using web_search
Step 2: Read repo/STATUS.md for current project status
Step 3: Read repo/IAN_TODO.md for pending human action items
Step 4: List all notebooks in repo/notebooks/ and note which tracks are covered (metacognition, learning, attention, exec functions, social cognition)
Step 5: Check repo/results/ — read FRONTIER_MODEL_RESULTS.md and SPOT_TEST_ANALYSIS.md for existing results
Step 6: Check which notebooks are already on Kaggle by reading any upload logs or status trackers in the repo
Step 7: Write a prioritized action plan to sub-workflows/metacognition/SURVEY.md covering: what is done, what is missing, what remaining days should focus on, what agent can do vs what needs Ian

description: Audit metacognition notebooks for kbench SDK compatibility and fix any issues
steps: Step 1: Read the kbench SDK cookbook at repo/research/kaggle_benchmarks_cookbook.md (or search repo for SDK reference docs)

Step 2: For each metacognition notebook (metacog_*.ipynb) in repo/notebooks/, verify: correct @kbench.task() decorator usage, proper return types (bool/float/tuple), valid llm.prompt() calls, dataset loaded via .evaluate() pattern
Step 3: Check that each notebook has exactly one %choose cell at the end selecting the main task
Step 4: List any issues found per notebook in a summary. For each issue, note the cell number and what needs fixing
Step 5: Fix any compatibility issues found directly in the notebook files
Step 6: Write a brief validation report to repo/results/metacog_sdk_audit.md

description: Review and strengthen contamination resistance across all metacognition benchmarks
steps: Step 1: Read repo/notebooks/metacog_canary.ipynb to understand the contamination canary approach

Step 2: For each metacognition benchmark (calibration, control, epistemic_humility, epistemic_revision, error_detection, fok, jol, learning_monitoring), examine the dataset/prompts for memorization vulnerability
Step 3: Check if any benchmark uses well-known trivia, famous examples, or content likely in training data
Step 4: For benchmarks with contamination risk, propose specific modifications: novel stimuli, procedurally generated items, or domain-shifted versions
Step 5: Implement the highest-priority contamination fixes (at least 2 benchmarks)
Step 6: Document changes and rationale in repo/results/contamination_hardening_log.md

description: Analyze spot test results and identify benchmarks that need difficulty calibration
steps: Step 1: Read repo/results/SPOT_TEST_ANALYSIS.md and repo/results/FRONTIER_MODEL_RESULTS.md for existing test data
Step 2: Read any JSON results files in repo/results/ (correlation_analysis.json, mock_validation.json, etc.)
Step 3: Identify benchmarks where models score too high (>90% — ceiling effect) or too low (<10% — floor effect)
Step 4: For ceiling-effect benchmarks, propose specific difficulty increases (harder items, more distractors, stricter scoring)
Step 5: For floor-effect benchmarks, propose simplifications or check if the task is testing the right thing
Step 6: Write analysis and recommendations to repo/results/difficulty_calibration_report.md

description: Improve SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md with stronger cognitive science citations and differentiation from CASK
steps: Step 1: Read repo/SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md for the current writeup
Step 2: Read repo/research/competition_landscape.md for CASK and competitor analysis
Step 3: Search web for 3-5 key cognitive science papers on metacognitive monitoring (FOK, JOL, calibration) published 2020-2025
Step 4: Add specific citations and theoretical grounding for each metacognition benchmark in the narrative
Step 5: Strengthen the differentiation section explaining how our benchmarks differ from CASK (which tests 17 models but uses simpler paradigms)
Step 6: Ensure the narrative highlights our unique features: contamination canaries, sub-metric decomposition, procedural generation

description: Fix inverted scoring in FOK, JOL, Calibration, and Canary benchmarks using Brier skill score
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_fok.py, task_jol.py, task_calibration.py, task_canary.py — find scoring formulas (likely 1-ECE)
Step 2: Replace 1-ECE with Brier skill score (BSS = 1 - BS/BS_ref) where BS_ref is climatological baseline. This rewards both calibration and resolution
Step 3: Validate with mock agents: perfect metacognitor scores >0.8, always-uncertain baseline scores <0.3, random baseline near 0
Step 4: Update matching notebooks in repo/notebooks/ (metacog_fok.ipynb, metacog_jol.ipynb, metacog_calibration.ipynb, metacog_canary.ipynb)
Step 5: Run mock validation script and confirm inversion is resolved; add scoring rationale comments to each modified file

description: Fix import errors in attention_vigilance, learning_curriculum, and attention_instruction_update benchmarks
steps: Step 1: Run python3 -c "import repo.benchmarks.attention.task_vigilance" (and similar) to reproduce the from data import errors
Step 2: Inspect each failing file to find the broken import paths (likely relative imports like from data import X)
Step 3: Fix imports to use correct relative or absolute paths matching the repo structure
Step 4: Verify each benchmark loads without errors: python3 -c "import ..." for all three
Step 5: Run a quick smoke test on each to confirm they produce valid output

description: Fix learning_interference benchmark scoring so it discriminates between different interference strategies
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/metacognition/task_learning_monitoring.py (or the learning interference task file) to understand why all 4 mock strategies score 0.4
Step 2: Redesign scoring to measure proactive and retroactive interference magnitude relative to a no-interference baseline
Step 3: Implement new scoring: baseline_accuracy - interference_accuracy = interference_magnitude; normalize to 0-1 scale
Step 4: Validate that at least 3 of 4 mock strategies produce distinct scores with >0.1 separation
Step 5: Update the corresponding notebook and add test cases

description: Replace CRT classic items with procedurally generated cognitive reflection variants to eliminate contamination
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/metacognition/ or repo/benchmarks/executive_functions/ for the CRT benchmark file
Step 2: Identify the classic CRT items (bat-and-ball, widget, lily pad) that models score 100% on
Step 3: Design 15 novel CRT-style items using the same cognitive trap patterns (intuitive-but-wrong answer) but with new scenarios and numbers
Step 4: Implement a procedural generator that randomizes numeric parameters for each item so exact answers differ per run
Step 5: Update the notebook, verify that items still have clear intuitive-wrong and reflective-correct answers
Step 6: Run a quick model test (or mock test) to confirm scores drop below 90%

description: Retry Kaggle API notebook pushes for the 18 API-blocked notebooks now that rate limit may have recovered
steps: Step 1: Read repo/CB_SUBMISSION_GUIDE.md and any upload tracking files to identify which 18 notebooks failed API push
Step 2: Test rate limit recovery with one small notebook push: kaggle kernels push on a test notebook
Step 3: If push succeeds, push remaining notebooks in batches of 3 with 60-second delays between batches
Step 4: Track success/failure for each notebook in repo/results/kaggle_push_status.md
Step 5: For any still-failing notebooks, note them as requiring manual web UI upload by Ian

description: Run all 9 metacognition benchmarks against Claude Sonnet via Bedrock and record real model scores
steps: Step 1: Read repo/scripts/run_benchmark_local.py to understand the local runner interface
Step 2: Activate the venv: source repo/.venv/bin/activate

Step 3: Run each of the 9 metacognition benchmarks (task_calibration, task_canary, task_epistemic_humility, task_epistemic_revision, task_error_detection, task_fok, task_jol, task_learning_monitoring, task_metacognitive_control) using the local runner with Bedrock Claude Sonnet (amazon-bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6)
Step 4: For each benchmark, record: task name, score, sub-metric breakdown, any errors or timeouts
Step 5: Save all results to repo/results/metacog_bedrock_scores.json with structure {task: {score, sub_metrics, model, timestamp}}
Step 6: Update repo/results/FRONTIER_MODEL_RESULTS.md metacognition section with the real scores in a markdown table

description: Retry Kaggle API push for 18 rate-limited notebooks with batched delays
steps: Step 1: List all notebook directories under repo/notebooks/ that have kernel-metadata.json files
Step 2: Cross-reference with KNOWLEDGE entries to identify the 18 unpushed notebooks (20/26 were pushed previously, 6 remained private)
Step 3: Test rate limit recovery: push one small notebook (e.g. metacog_canary) via kaggle kernels push -p repo/notebooks/metacog_canary/
Step 4: If successful, push remaining notebooks in batches of 3, waiting 60 seconds between each batch
Step 5: Log each push result (success/429/other error) to repo/results/kaggle_push_status_v2.md
Step 6: For any still-failing notebooks, add them to repo/IAN_TODO.md under a manual upload section

description: Update SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md with real Bedrock model scores replacing placeholder text
steps: Step 1: Read repo/results/metacog_bedrock_scores.json (produced by earlier task) for real model scores
Step 2: Read repo/SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md and locate all placeholder/empty score sections
Step 3: Replace placeholder text in the metacognition results section with actual Claude Sonnet scores, including per-benchmark scores and sub-metric breakdowns
Step 4: Add a Model Performance Summary table showing all 9 metacognition benchmarks with scores
Step 5: Update any claims about model behavior (e.g., calibration failure, ceiling effects) with evidence from the real scores
Step 6: Ensure the narrative reads coherently with the new data — no dangling references to missing results

description: Create a consolidated IAN_TODO_FINAL.md with step-by-step CB submission checklist for Ian
steps: Step 1: Read repo/IAN_TODO.md and repo/CB_SUBMISSION_GUIDE.md for existing instructions
Step 2: Read repo/results/kaggle_push_status.md (and v2 if exists) to identify which notebooks still need manual upload

Step 3: Create repo/IAN_TODO_FINAL.md with a numbered checklist: (a) toggle private notebooks to public via web UI, (b) delete ghost entries, (c) register each public notebook as a CB task at kaggle.com/benchmarks/tasks/new, (d) post discussion thread using KAGGLE_DISCUSSION_DRAFT.md
Step 4: For each CB task registration, include the exact notebook URL, task name, and track (metacognition/learning/attention/exec_func/social_cog)
Step 5: Estimate time per step so Ian can plan the ~1.5hrs of manual work
Step 6: Add a verification checklist at the end: how to confirm each benchmark is live on CB platform

description: Run psychometric validation on real Bedrock scores to verify benchmark quality claims
steps: Step 1: Load repo/results/metacog_bedrock_scores.json with real model scores
Step 2: For benchmarks with sub-metrics (FOK, JOL, error_detection), compute inter-item consistency (Cronbach alpha) from individual item responses if available
Step 3: Compute discriminant validity: within-track score variance vs between-track variance for metacognition benchmarks
Step 4: Check for ceiling effects (score >0.90) and floor effects (score <0.10) across all 9 benchmarks
Step 5: Verify BSS scoring produces expected ordering: perfect>partial>random>inverse for any benchmarks where mock data is available
Step 6: Save psychometric report to repo/results/psychometric_validation_bedrock.md with tables and pass/fail on each criterion
